title: Garlic Steak & Broccoli Bowls with Herbed Cottage Cheese
displayTitle: Garlic Steak & Broccoli Bowls with Herbed Cottage Cheese
seoTitle: Garlic Steak & Broccoli Bowls with Herbed Cottage Cheese | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Seared steak strips and roasted broccoli over rice with a garlic-herb cottage cheese sauce
subtitle: Seared steak strips and roasted broccoli over rice with a garlic-herb cottage cheese sauce
description: Seared sirloin strips and roasted broccoli sit over rice, finished with a smooth garlic-herb cottage cheese sauce blended until creamy. It reads like a steakhouse plate with a real per-serving protein boost.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice, bring it with water to a boil in a lidded pot, then reduce to low and simmer 18 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then fluff.

steps.title: Roast the broccoli
steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss broccoli with oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan and roast 15–18 minutes until browned at the tips and crisp-tender. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Blend the cottage cheese sauce
steps.instruction: Blend cottage cheese, garlic, chives, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt until completely smooth. Thin with a splash of water if it's too thick to drizzle.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.instruction: Pat steak strips dry and season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Sear in a very hot skillet in batches, 60–90 seconds per side, until browned outside and medium-rare to medium inside.

steps.title: Rest the steak
steps.instruction: Rest steak 5 minutes on a plate before serving — cutting or plating it immediately loses the juices onto the board instead of the bowl.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Layer rice and broccoli in each bowl, top with seared steak strips, and finish with a generous drizzle of the garlic-herb cottage cheese sauce.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover seared steak strips — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool seared steak strips and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Slice steak thin and against the grain so it stays tender through a fast, hot sear.
Rookie tip: Blend the cottage cheese sauce until fully smooth — a few seconds longer than you think it needs.
Use flank or flat iron steak as a budget-friendly swap for sirloin.
Keep the skillet very hot; thin steak strips need speed more than time.
tonightSpread: Main: Garlic steak and broccoli bowls
Sides: Simple green salad, crusty bread
Condiments: Extra cottage cheese sauce, hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool seared steak strips in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Reheat steak gently in a covered skillet rather than the microwave to avoid overcooking it further.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It gives steak-night fans a genuine reason to try cottage cheese — blended smooth, it tastes like a herb sauce, not a diet ingredient — while keeping the protein count well above a normal steak dinner.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: the cottage cheese sauce holds 4 days blended and covered. Storage: keep steak, rice, broccoli, and sauce in separate containers up to 3 days. Reheating: reheat steak and rice to 165°F; add sauce cold or gently warmed, never boiled.
substitutions: Use flank steak or flat iron steak instead of sirloin.
Use Greek yogurt instead of cottage cheese for the sauce.
Use cauliflower rice for a lower-carb base.
